responses: My final position advocates for a balanced and human-centered allocation of Riverton Industries' $5 million AI transition budget, prioritizing workforce training at 33% to ensure employees are equipped for new roles, and employee support at 22% to address transition challenges and mental health. I support cautious but meaningful investment in automation at 23% to improve manufacturing efficiency without overwhelming the workforce, alongside 12% for data infrastructure to build a resilient technological foundation, and 10% for innovation to foster new AI-driven products. Crucially, I emphasize embedding adaptive, integrated governance with clear metrics and frontline feedback across all areas to ensure ethical oversight, agility, and alignment with both human and technical priorities throughout the transition.

I would recommend allocating the $5 million AI transition budget with a strong emphasis on workforce training (around 33%) and employee support (about 22%) to ensure our employees are equipped and supported through this major change, fostering trust and minimizing disruption. Automation should be funded cautiously at approximately 23% to drive efficiency gains without overwhelming the workforce or risking premature adoption. Data infrastructure deserves a solid 12-15% to build the technical foundation necessary for scalable, secure AI deployment, while innovation can be set at 10% to encourage new product development and experimentation. Crucially, I advise embedding adaptive, transparent governance and ethical oversight across all areas to ensure accountability, responsiveness, and alignment with our human-centered values throughout the transition. This balanced approach reflects both the competitive need to modernize and the imperative to support our people effectively.

I would explain that my view on Riverton Industries' AI transition budget is centered on balancing technological advancement with strong support for our workforce. I believe we should prioritize workforce training and employee support to ensure our people are prepared and cared for during this change, allocating roughly a third of the budget to training and about a fifth to support services. At the same time, we need to invest cautiously in automation to improve efficiency without causing disruption, while also strengthening our data infrastructure and innovation efforts to build a resilient, future-ready foundation. Importantly, I advocate embedding adaptive governance and ethical oversight across all areas to ensure transparency, accountability, and responsiveness throughout the transition. This balanced, human-centered approach aims to drive sustainable success for both our employees and the company.
